// Ids of the berths the boat could be given now, shortest berth first.
// Berths of equal length keep their order in `berths`.
export function berthsFor(boat: Boat, berths: Berth[], needPower: boolean): BerthId[] {
    return berths
        .map((berth, index) => ({ berth, index }))
        .filter(({ berth }) => isFree(berth) && fits(boat, berth) && (!needPower || berth.power))
        .sort((a, b) => a.berth.length - b.berth.length || a.index - b.index)
        .map(({ berth }) => berth.id);
}

I added `berthsFor` at the end of `src/moorings.ts`. It keeps free berths the boat fits by `fits`, requires power only when `needPower` is true, and sorts by length with the original index as tie-breaker. It builds new arrays and never modifies `berths` or any berth. I'm not unsure about anything.
